I do like O Fortuna, but I'm tired of hearing it and tired of singing it, because the alto part at least is extremely dull. The only interesting moments are finding the somewhat counter-intuitive first note from the opening chord (which I still have to think about to get right despite singing it many times) and the rhythm in the non-soprano parts in the last line being different to the very prominent soprano rhythm and thus difficult to count correctly. Other than that it's pretty boring to sing and that means choirs struggle to maintain the intensity during the low volume bits without gradually getting louder, so it's usually far less effective than it should be.
 
Completely unrelated to theme music, but the third movement of Carmina Burana is called Veris leta facies and it's simple and beautiful and graceful and it's my favourite movement in the whole piece, and deserves to be heard more. I also like the ones about drinking and sex and the tenor solo as a swan singing about how he's been killed, cooked and eaten.
